_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution. `s.fem.fem2d` is a semio-NATIVE structural MODEL — nine id-keyed collections and one settings record — and its vocabulary edits the model, never the analysis, so a finite-element solver has nothing to adjudicate. The reference is a SECOND IMPLEMENTATION in Python written from this subset's committed snapshot schema, mutation grammar and specification vectors.

oracles.rationale:
A second implementation of the `s.fem.fem2d` model and all twenty-five typed mutations, in Python, at `../../../../../🧪️tests/mutate-fem2d-1/🐍️component.py`. Written from `../🧬️schema/📸️snapshot/🔣️.json` (the nine members and the analysis settings record), `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/📝️text/📖️.grammar.semio` (the twenty-five verbs) and the twenty-five committed `(before, mutation, after, outcome)` specification vectors — which is also where the RECORD shapes and the cascade rules are actually written down. It imports nothing from this repository and transliterates none of its Rust. A third-party library was declined, not merely absent: `code_aster`, `OpenSees`, `anastruct` and `PyNite` compute displacements and forces FROM a model, while every one of the twenty-five kinds edits the model document itself — `replace-section` swaps a profile record, `add-load` appends to a case's load list, `change-load-case-self-weight` flips a boolean — and none of them reads `.dsl.semio`. DEFECT FOUND WHILE WRITING IT, reported rather than worked around: `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/🔣️.json` is a verbatim copy of the SNAPSHOT schema with the title changed, and in the snapshot schema every one of `FemNode`, `FemElement`, `FemRegion`, `FemMaterial`, `FemSection`, `FemSupport`, `FemLoadCase` and `FemCombination` is an EMPTY object with no properties at all. `package` is deliberately empty: the implementation needs no distribution, so this entry contributes nothing to `🔒️dependencies.json`.

UNDER PROTOCOL V2 this registration is classified `cross-semio-implementation` — a required SUPPLEMENTAL oracle that does not discharge `fem2d-1-mutate`'s external-oracle requirement for its 25-kind mutation vocabulary; a qualifying third-party reference (`third-party-library` / `third-party-cli` / `standards-reference-tool`) is still owed.

🕸️ THE CARRIER READER, REGISTERED AGAINST EXACTLY THREE OF THIS SUBSET'S TWENTY-FIVE KINDS, AND THE SCOPE IS THE WHOLE POINT. STEP 0 first: `../🚪️io/📤️export/🧵️serializers/🗿️artifacts/🧊️obj/🔖️3.0/✳️any/🦀️.rs` and the sibling `🟪️stl/🔖️ascii/✳️any/🦀️.rs` both triangulate every `FemRegion`'s footprint (`crate::fem2d_engine::meshing::build_semio_mesh_snapshot`), extrude it by the region's OWN thickness, split to tets and take the boundary faces, then hand that to stdio's real, already-oracled `s.stdio.semio@v1/✳️mesh` bridge and `encode_obj`/`encode_stl_ascii` grammar — neither leaf returns `print_dsl(..).into_bytes()` under a foreign extension, so both are REAL carriers, not stubs. `three` parses them with no knowledge of our snapshot type, so what it recovers from the bytes is an independent reading rather than our own encoder agreeing with itself.

WHAT IT DISCHARGES. `create-region`, `replace-region` and `delete-region` are the only three of this subset's twenty-five kinds that move a vertex a carrier can see: `build_semio_mesh_snapshot` reads only `region.{outline, holes and thickness}` and consults nothing else on the document. Materials, sections, nodes, `Bar/Beam` elements (no cross-section PROFILE, so no honest 3D solid — see the bridge fn's own doc), supports, load cases, loads, combinations and analysis settings are INVISIBLE in OBJ/STL BY CONSTRUCTION and carry no `oracleRequirement` this entry discharges — see `fem2d-1-mutate-uncarried` and the `noOracleDecisions` entry below.

MEASURED, both ways, with the sibling `manifold-3d` oracle doing the arithmetic (`🔬️probes/📜️script.ts mesh-compare`): the SAME shape exported to OBJ and re-imported through both loaders compares at relativeVolumeError 0.000e+00, relativeAreaError 0.000e+00 and normalizedSymmetricHausdorff 0.000e+00; a genuinely different region (a hole added, a different footprint, a different scale) separates at relativeVolumeError up to 7.083e-01 and normalizedSymmetricHausdorff up to 1.242. A FINDING FROM BUILDING THIS: relativeVolumeError and genus are translation-invariant, so a defect that moves the whole region to the wrong place without changing its shape — e.g. a `replace-region` that silently drops `the region has no elevation field` — passes relativeVolumeError at ~1.269e-16 and genusEqual true; only normalizedSymmetricHausdorff catches it, measured at 4.465e-01 for the same-shape-wrong-elevation pair this oracle's own fixture corpus records (`solid-one-hole` vs `solid-one-hole-elevated-low`). The gate therefore asserts on BOTH metrics, never volume alone.

productionDebt.reason: three is already a production-runtime dependency of ✏️s/🔌️plugins/📐️cad, 🧩️puzzle and the os renderer, so this oracle is NOT isolated from production the way manifold-3d is.
productionDebt.consequence: A bug shared between three's loaders and a production consumer of three would not be caught by this oracle alone. The independence this pilot actually rests on is the measuring half, manifold-3d, which is test-only and a different engine family; three is the parser, manifold is the judge.

oracles.rationale:
📏️ THE MEASURING ENGINE, AND A DIFFERENT FAMILY FROM THE READER ON PURPOSE. `three` parses the OBJ/STL carrier; manifold-3d computes volume, surface area and genus from what `three` recovered, and — via its own `CrossSection.extrude` — is ALSO what `../🏭️generator/📜️script.ts` uses to independently BUILD every fixture's expected geometry: a real solid-boolean kernel's native polygon-with-holes extrusion, not a re-derivation of `crate::mesh::triangulate`/`extrude_tri_mesh`/`split_to_tets`/`boundary_faces`. Because the reader and the judge are independent implementations, the measurement checks the parse instead of confirming it.

manifold-3d requires a welded, watertight mesh and REFUSES a triangle soup outright, which OBJ and STL both are. Welding is therefore not a tidying step but a precondition, done on a grid keyed to the model's OWN bounding-box diagonal (1e-7 relative) rather than a constant — the `scale` family in `../🏭️generator/📜️script.ts` proves this holds from 1e-3 to 1e6× a metre-scale region.

WHY THE GATE IS NEAR-EXACT RATHER THAN TESSELLATION-TOLERANT (the opposite choice from the STEP/BRep pilot, and deliberately so): every region here is a STRAIGHT-EDGED polygon (outline ± holes) extruded LINEARLY — no curvature anywhere in `build_semio_mesh_snapshot` — so volume and surface area of a flat-faced prism are triangulation-INVARIANT. A polygon triangulated one way by our own `crate::mesh::triangulate` and another way by manifold-3d's `CrossSection.extrude` integrates to the SAME value either way. MEASURED: this corpus's own `expected.metrics.json` compares manifold-3d's measured volume against an independent shoelace-formula analytic volume for every non-degenerate recipe and finds agreement to 1e-8–1e-16 relative error — floating-point noise, not tessellation disagreement — which is what licenses a near-exact gate here where the mesh pilot itself gates near-exact for a different reason (the artifact IS the vertex buffer there) and the BRep pilot gates loose (real curvature there).

A through-hole is a genuine TOPOLOGICAL fact under this gate, not merely a triangle count: an n-hole region measures genus n regardless of which engine triangulated it, exactly as the mesh pilot's bored cube established for a curved solid.

📖️ A READER over a DIFFERENT CARRIER, which is why it covers what the two mesh oracles cannot.

`three-fem2d-mesh-reader` and `manifold-fem2d-mesh-measure` read the STL/OBJ export, so they witness GEOMETRY. A material's Young's modulus, a section's second moment of area, a support's restrained DOFs, a load case's self-weight flag and the analysis settings do not move a single triangle — which is exactly why 22 of this subset's kinds were recorded `-uncarried` against those two. That label was honest about the MESH carrier and does not generalise.

This subset's JSON export is not a stub. Unlike its csv/md/txt leaves, which wrap the DSL text in a single blob, its json leaf emits `serde_json::to_value(snapshot)` — the real structured tree, every snapshot field. So all nine collections are carrier-level facts and a third-party JSON implementation witnesses every one of them.

This is the same shape as the accepted `quick-xml`/svg and `burntsushi-csv`/mathematical readers: the judge is a third-party implementation of the CARRIER, and nothing in this repository predicts the answer it is judging. The expected state is the committed `after` half of each fixture.

noOracleDecisions.rationale:
🧱 Twenty-two of this subset's twenty-five mutations edit a field `build_semio_mesh_snapshot` never reads: materials, sections, nodes, `Bar/Beam` elements (`area`/`iy` are scalar section properties, not a cross-section PROFILE, so no honest 3D solid can be derived from a bar/beam — see the bridge fn's own doc), supports, load cases, individual loads, combinations and analysis settings. `build_semio_mesh_snapshot` reads only `region.{outline, holes and thickness}` and nothing else on `Fem2dSnapshot` — a mesh carrier sees geometry, not solver settings or materials, and this repository's OBJ/STL leaves for this subset encode nothing else. `../🔬️probes/📜️script.ts` is never even asked about these kinds; there is no `unsupported` branch for them because they are not wired to a carrier at all.

A third-party FE SOLVER was surveyed and declined for the same reason `fem2d-python-independent`'s own rationale already gives: `code_aster`, `OpenSees`, `anastruct` and `PyNite` compute displacements and forces FROM a model, while every one of these twenty-two kinds edits the model DOCUMENT itself and none of them reads a solved result. That survey stands for this decision too; it is not re-litigated here.

WHAT DISCHARGES THESE TODAY: only `fem2d-python-independent`, a `cross-semio-implementation` — a required SUPPLEMENTAL oracle, never a substitute per protocol v2. A qualifying third-party reference for `fem2d-1-mutate-uncarried` is still owed and is recorded here as a debt, not a verdict: these twenty-two kinds report honestly as un-oracled via the `oracleRequirements` naming `fem2d-1-mutate-uncarried` in `mutationManifests` below, rather than being silently absorbed into `fem2d-1-mutate`'s three-kind geometry coverage.

comparisonProfiles.description: The nine snapshot collections as ordered lists — nodes, elements, regions, materials, sections, supports, loadCases, combinations, analysis — canonicalised with object keys sorted and array order preserved, so a reordering is a difference rather than a tie.

The extruded-region mesh measurement bundle (expected-obj + expected-stl + expected-measurements, one `manifold-fem2d-mesh-measure` fixture per `replace-region-geometry` vector) compared on its TRIANGULATION-INVARIANT topological facts only: `empty`, `solids` (connected-component count), `genus`/`componentGenus`/`expectedGenus` (surface genus — a miscounted hole or wrong connectivity fails here even when two independent triangulators tile the SAME flat-faced polygon differently) and `crossFormatTriangleCountsAgree` (the fixture's own OBJ/STL self-consistency flag). Every DIMENSIONAL field is stripped from this flat structural equality and left to the paired `fem-polygon-exact` tolerance profile instead: `vertexCount`/`triangleCount`/`weld.soupVertices`/`weld.weldedVertices`/`weld.droppedDegenerateTriangles`/`crossFormatTriangleCounts` (triangulation is producer freedom for a flat-faced prism — this subset's own `🔬️probes/📜️script.ts` `compareMeshes` gate documents that 'volume and area are triangulation-invariant... unlike a curved BRep solid'), `volume`/`surfaceArea`/`boundingBox`/`boundingBoxDiagonal`/`weld.grid`/`analyticVolume`/`analyticVolumeRelativeError`/`analyticMinZ`/`minZRelativeError`/`expectedBaseZ` and the purely descriptive `measuredFrom`. A single flat comparison tolerance cannot honestly serve fixtures spanning a boundingBoxDiagonal of 4.5 mm to 4.5 Mm (nine orders of magnitude) in this subset's own corpus, which is why the dimensional half is a NAMED, scale-relative tolerance profile rather than a number on this spec.

toleranceProfiles.description: Straight-edged, flat-faced FEM region meshes (a linear extrusion of a polygon outline+holes by the region's own thickness — no curvature anywhere in `build_semio_mesh_snapshot`'s bridge), re-imported from float32 STL/OBJ and welded onto a `boundingBoxDiagonal × 1e-7` grid. Derived from THIS subset's own fixture corpus (12 `expected.metrics.json` files spanning `boundingBoxDiagonal` 1.42 to 4.48 and the paired 🧊️3d corpus down to 4.48e-3 and up to 4.48e6): the worst observed float32 round-trip noise across every fixture is `analyticVolumeRelativeError` 2.04e-6 and `minZRelativeError` 2.12e-8, both at the smallest (1e-3) scale fixture; the weld grid itself is `diagonal × 1e-7` at every single scale, by construction. `relativeLength`/`relativeArea`/`relativeVolume` are set to 1e-6/1e-5/1e-5 — a comfortable ≥10× margin over that measured noise floor. `absoluteLength`/`absoluteArea`/`absoluteVolume` floor at 1e-9 for near-zero references, matching the smallest fixture's own weld grid (1e-9, at the 1e-3 scale). A genuine defect sits nowhere near this floor: this subset's own carrier-oracle rationale (`three-fem2d-mesh-reader` entry, this same file) measures `relativeVolumeError` up to 7.083e-1 for a structurally different region, and `normalizedSymmetricHausdorff` at 4.465e-1 even for the SUBTLEST real defect on record (same shape, wrong elevation, where the elevation-invariant volume/area metrics read ~0) — so `normalizedHausdorffMax`/`normalizedCentroidDistanceMax` are set to 1e-4: roughly four thousand times below that smallest real signal, and roughly a hundred times above the representation noise floor. `maxOverrideFactor: 5` matches the CORE `mechanical-standard`/`large-coordinate` profiles' own headroom, reserved for a future fixture whose own measured baseline needs a documented, capped exception rather than a silently widened gate.

comparisonPipelines.description: Carrier-level equality over the nine snapshot collections, read through serde_json. GATING for the kinds the mesh oracles structurally cannot witness.
